literal: Xie's household chief of the gentlemen Wei Yan and former gate guard Gaozu Zhen hoped for Zhao's promotion and framed the affair.
idiomatic: Xie's household chief Wei Yan and former gate guard Gaozu Zhen, hoping for Zhao's favor, framed the affair.

literal: At first Zhao ordered Palace Attendant Yuan Hui to memorialize Shizong; Hui would not follow; he ordered Left Guard Yuan Zhen to speak.
idiomatic: Zhao first had Palace Attendant Yuan Hui report to Shizong; Hui refused; he had Left Guard Yuan Zhen speak instead.

literal: Shizong inquired of Hui; Hui made clear Xie had no such thing.
idiomatic: Shizong asked Hui, who made clear Xie had done no such thing.

literal: Shizong again asked Zhao; Zhao used Wei Yan and Zhen as proof; Shizong then believed it.
idiomatic: Shizong asked Zhao again; Zhao cited Wei Yan and Zhen as proof, and Shizong believed.

literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Yongping, Xie and Prince Yong of Gaoyang, Prince Jia of Guangyang, Prince Yi of Qinghe, Prince Huai of Guangping, and Gao Zhao and others were summoned in.
idiomatic: In Yongping year 1, ninth month, Xie and Princes Yong of Gaoyang, Jia of Guangyang, Yi of Qinghe, Huai of Guangping, and Gao Zhao were summoned.

literal: At that time Xie's consort was in childbirth; Xie therefore firmly refused and did not go.
idiomatic: His consort was in childbirth; he firmly refused to go.

literal: Palace envoys came in succession; having no way out he ordered the carriage; his mind was very fearful and anxious; he took leave of his consort and mounted the carriage.
idiomatic: Envoys came one after another; he had no choice but to order the carriage, fearful and anxious, and took leave of his consort before mounting.

literal: Entering the Eastern Flank Gate, crossing a small bridge, the ox would not advance; they struck it a long while.
idiomatic: At the Eastern Flank Gate his ox would not cross a small bridge though they beat it long.

literal: Again an envoy blamed Xie for coming late; he was ordered to remove the ox; men pulled the carriage forward; they feasted in the forbidden precinct.
idiomatic: Another envoy blamed his lateness; the ox was removed and men pulled him in; they feasted within the palace.

literal: By night all were drunk; each went to a separate lodging to rest.
idiomatic: By night all were drunk and each went to a separate room to rest.

literal: Soon Yuan Zhen led warriors bearing poisoned wine and arrived.
idiomatic: Soon Yuan Zhen came with warriors bearing poisoned wine.

literal: Xie said: "I am loyal to the court—what crime brings killing!"
idiomatic: Xie said: "I am loyal to the court—what crime brings death?"

literal: "If I may once see the Supreme One, I die without regret."
idiomatic: "Let me see the emperor once and I die without regret."

literal: Zhen said: "The Supreme One—how can he be seen again!"
idiomatic: Zhen said: "The emperor—how can you see him again?"

literal: "The King need only drink the wine."
idiomatic: "Only drink."

literal: Xie said: "The Supreme One is sage and bright; he ought not kill me without cause—I beg to face once the one who reports my crime and settle right and wrong."
idiomatic: Xie said: "The emperor is sage and bright; he should not kill me without cause—let me face my accuser once and settle right and wrong."

literal: The warriors struck Xie twice with the ring of the blade.
idiomatic: The warriors struck him twice with the ring of the blade.

literal: Xie cried aloud: "Heaven!"
idiomatic: Xie cried: "Heaven!"

literal: Loyal yet killed.
idiomatic: Loyal—and killed.

literal: The warriors again struck Xie with the ring of the blade.
idiomatic: They struck him again with the ring.

literal: Xie then drank the poisoned wine; the warriors thereupon killed him.
idiomatic: He drank the poison; the warriors then killed him.

literal: Toward dawn they wrapped the corpse in a quilt, carried it out through the screen gate, loaded the corpse back to his residence, saying the king had died from drink.
idiomatic: At dawn they wrapped the corpse, carried it out the screen gate, and sent it home saying the king had died from drink.

literal: Xie's consort Lady Li, daughter of Minister of Works Chong, wailed aloud: "Gao Zhao killed a man against reason; Heaven has spirit—you will yet die an evil death."
idiomatic: Consort Lady Li, daughter of Minister Chong, wailed: "Gao Zhao killed against reason; Heaven has spirit—you will yet die wickedly."

literal: When Zhao was killed for his crime, discussers knew there was retribution.
idiomatic: When Zhao was killed for his crimes, men said retribution had come.

literal: Shizong held mourning for him at the Eastern Hall, gave Eastern Garden first-grade secret vessels, one suit of court dress, eighty myriad in condolence money, two thousand bolts of cloth, five hundred jin of wax; the Grand Herald oversaw the funeral.
idiomatic: Shizong mourned him in the Eastern Hall and gave Eastern Garden rites, court dress, eighty myriad cash, two thousand bolts of cloth, five hundred jin of wax; the Grand Herald oversaw the funeral.

literal: Xie had great merit for the state yet was killed without crime; the common people resented it.
idiomatic: Xie had served the state greatly yet was killed without crime; the people resented it.

literal: Travelers, men and women, wept as they spoke: "Chief Minister Gao wrongly killed so worthy a king!"
idiomatic: Men and women on the road wept and said: "Chief Minister Gao wrongly killed so worthy a king!"

literal: At court, noble and base alike, none did not lose spirit.
idiomatic: At court, high and low alike lost heart.

literal: Posthumous honors: Acting Yellow Battle-Ax, Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without, Duke Minister over the Masses, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Prince as before.
idiomatic: He was posthumously given acting yellow battle-ax, bearer of the staff, commander of all armies, duke minister over the masses, palace attendant, and grand preceptor, prince as before.

literal: Given imperial carriage with nine tassels, a hundred tiger guards with swords of state, front and rear feathered canopy and drum escort, and covered funeral carriage.
idiomatic: They gave him the imperial carriage with nine tassels, a hundred tiger guards with swords of state, front and rear feathered escort, and covered funeral carriage.

literal: The relevant office memorialized that Minister of Rites Liu Fang discussed Xie's posthumous name, saying: "The King from youth raised virtue; he was born with utmost filiality; keen nature surpassed others; learning needed no teacher."
idiomatic: The relevant office reported Minister Liu Fang's posthumous proposal: "The king from youth raised virtue, born to utmost filiality, keen beyond others, learning without teachers."

literal: Outstanding conduct sprang from the natural;
idiomatic: Outstanding conduct sprang from nature;

literal: uncommon beauty, in youth alone emerging.
idiomatic: uncommon beauty emerged alone in youth.

literal: When he entered to share government, the imperial commands had luster;
idiomatic: Entering government, his commands shone;

literal: ascending the central axis, he spread and clarified the five teachings.
idiomatic: on the central axis he spread the five teachings.

literal: North of Han reported danger; the emperor sternly inquired into guilt; the King inwardly attended the medicine and broth, outwardly commanded the six armies.
idiomatic: When the north of Han cried danger the emperor asked guilt; inwardly he tended the broth, outwardly he commanded the six armies.

literal: When the imperial carriage peacefully halted, above and below were mournful and wretched.
idiomatic: When the imperial carriage halted, court and realm mourned.

literal: Fierce and bold he bore grief; heroic strategy flowed in secret; he winged and guarded the spirit carriage, arrayed the troops and shook the banners.
idiomatic: Fierce in grief, strategy flowing in secret, he guarded the spirit carriage and arrayed troops and banners.

literal: Stopping again and again from Wan to Luoyang, sending off and receiving the dwelling—without shame before Zhou and Huo; receiving the testament he became assistant; far and near were settled.
idiomatic: From Wan to Luoyang he sent off and received the dwelling without shame before Zhou and Huo; taking the testament he assisted until far and near were calm.

literal: Dividing Shaan and Heng regions, his praise flowed in Yan and Zhao;
idiomatic: Holding Shaan and Heng, praise flowed through Yan and Zhao;

literal: pacifying and quieting west of the river, his awe subdued the southern Yue.
idiomatic: pacifying the west of the river, his awe subdued the southern Yue.

literal: Entering to adjust the hundred duties, all achievements were bright; diligent in toil he did not weary; in merit he only grew more modest.
idiomatic: Adjusting the hundred duties, all achievements bright; tireless in toil, in merit he only grew more modest.

literal: Warm, respectful, harmonious, and kind; loyal, refined, and broad in benevolence; rising and dwelling had measure; he ended well because he began with depth.
idiomatic: Warm, respectful, harmonious, and kind; loyal, refined, and broad; measured in rising and dwelling; he ended as deeply as he began.

literal: Lofty was his heart; merit complete, his person withdrew.
idiomatic: Lofty in heart; merit complete, he withdrew.

literal: Righteousness brightened the sage breast; beauty lit the age's canon.
idiomatic: Righteousness lit the sage breast; beauty lit the age's canon.

literal: According to the posthumous law, preserving the great and settling merit is called "Martial"; good inquiry reaching everywhere is called "Proclaimer"; posthumous name: Prince Martial-Proclaimer.
idiomatic: By posthumous law, preserving the great and settling merit is Martial, good inquiry everywhere is Proclaimer—the posthumous name Prince Martial-Proclaimer.

literal: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, he was posthumously titled Emperor Wenmu; consort Lady Li was Empress Wenmu; the spirit tablet was moved to the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the temple name was Sizu.
idiomatic: When Zhuangdi took the throne he was posthumously Emperor Wenmu and Lady Li Empress Wenmu; the tablet entered the ancestral temple as Sizu.

literal: The account is in the biography of Prince Yu of Linhuai.
idiomatic: The account is in the biography of Prince Yu of Linhuai.

literal: In the time of the Former Deposed Emperor, his spirit tablet was removed.
idiomatic: Under the Former Deposed Emperor his tablet was removed.

literal: Shao, styled Shizhou, inherited.
idiomatic: Shao, styled Shizhou, succeeded.

literal: At the end of Wuding he was Si Province governor.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was Si Province governor.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, his rank was reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: When Northern Qi took the throne, his title was lowered per precedent.

literal: Shao's younger brother Xi, styled Shishao.
idiomatic: Shao's younger brother Xi, styled Shishao.

literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was enfeoffed Prince of Wu'an, fief of one thousand households.
idiomatic: Early in Wuding he was made Prince of Wu'an with a thousand-household fief.

literal: At the end of Wuding he was Secretariat Gentleman.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was secretariat gentleman.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, his rank was reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: When Northern Qi took the throne, his title was lowered per precedent.

literal: Shao's elder brother's son Zhi, styled Fangyan.
idiomatic: Shao's nephew Zhi, styled Fangyan.

literal: From youth he was known by name; the Literary Prince of Qinghe prized and loved him.
idiomatic: Known from youth, he was prized by the Literary Prince of Qinghe.

literal: At the start of his career he was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.
idiomatic: He began as regular attendant of scattered cavalry, then secretariat gentleman.

literal: Later he was made Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
idiomatic: Later he was regular attendant of direct communication, then gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling's edict said: "The late Grand Preceptor, Prince Martial-Proclaimer of Pengcheng—his Way was lofty, his virtue abundant; merit surpassed Weiguan; he matched the former court and guided the last charge."
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling wrote: "The late grand preceptor, Prince Martial-Proclaimer of Pengcheng—Way lofty, virtue abundant, merit past Weiguan, matched the former court and guided the last charge."

literal: "Supporting illness and rescuing difficulty, he showed the loyalty of north of Han;"
idiomatic: "Supporting illness and rescuing trouble, he showed loyalty north of Han;"

literal: "sending off and receiving the dwelling, he fulfilled the integrity of south of Lu."
idiomatic: "sending off and receiving the dwelling, he fulfilled the integrity south of Lu."

literal: "The altars relied on him for peace; the imperial foundation by him was forever firm."
idiomatic: "The altars leaned on him; the throne stood firm by him."

literal: "Yet humble light and keeping to covenant, he repeatedly waved off added fief rewards;"
idiomatic: "Yet humble and keeping covenant, he waved off added fiefs;"

literal: "declining much and accepting little, he finally kept the first grant's seal."
idiomatic: "declining much and taking little, he kept the first grant."

literal: "This is not what is called pursuing the old to repay kindness and remembering merit to repay virtue."
idiomatic: "That is not pursuing the old to repay kindness or remembering merit to repay virtue."

literal: "From the households enfeoffed before and after, separately enfeoff three sons as county dukes, each with a fief of one thousand households, hoping in small measure to comfort the benevolent soul and slightly declare the court's canon."
idiomatic: "From fiefs given before and after, enfeoff three sons as county dukes of a thousand households each, to comfort his soul and slightly declare the court's canon."

literal: Son Zhi was enfeoffed Duke of Zhending with an open state.
idiomatic: Zhi was enfeoffed Duke of Zhending with an open state.

literal: He went out as Champion General and Liang Province inspector.
idiomatic: He went out as champion general and Liang inspector.

literal: Before long he fell ill; he lingered at ease in Nanzheng without other achievement in government.
idiomatic: Soon he fell ill and lingered at ease in Nanzheng without other achievement.

literal: Summoned back to the capital, he died of illness.
idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he died of illness.

literal: Posthumously: Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the South, Director of the Ministry of Justice, Ji Province inspector.
idiomatic: Posthumously: regular attendant of scattered cavalry, general who pacifies the south, director of the ministry of justice, and Ji inspector.

literal: When Xiaozhuang took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Chenliu, fief of two thousand households, given Acting Yellow Battle-Ax, Grand Preceptor, Grand Marshal, Grand Commandant, and front and rear feathered canopy and drum escort.
idiomatic: At Xiaozhuang's accession he was posthumously Prince of Chenliu with two thousand households, acting yellow battle-ax, grand preceptor, grand marshal, and grand commandant, with feathered escort.

literal: Son Kuan, styled Simeng, inherited the princely rank.
idiomatic: Son Kuan, styled Simeng, inherited the title.

literal: He was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: He was regular attendant of scattered cavalry and general who pacifies the south.

literal: Soon he was made Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the Army.
idiomatic: Soon he was palace attendant and general who pacifies the army.

literal: In the third year of Yong'an, Erzhu Zhao killed him at Jinyang.
idiomatic: In Yong'an year 3 Erzhu Zhao killed him at Jinyang.

literal: He had no heir; the state was abolished.
idiomatic: He had no heir; the fief was abolished.

literal: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was posthumously given Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Commander of military affairs in Qing, Qi, and Ji provinces, Defender Grand General, Qing Province inspector; again posthumously Duke Minister over the Masses.
idiomatic: At the Deposed Emperor's accession he was posthumously bearer of the staff, scattered-cavalry attendant, commander of Qing, Qi, and Ji, defender grand general, and Qing inspector, then again duke minister over the masses.

literal: Younger brother Gang, styled Jinming.
idiomatic: Younger brother Gang, styled Jinming.

literal: At the beginning of Zhuangdi's reign he was enfeoffed Prince of Fuyang, fief of one thousand households.
idiomatic: At Zhuangdi's accession he was Prince of Fuyang with a thousand households.

literal: At the end of Wuding he was Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was vice director of the imperial clan court.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, his rank was reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: When Northern Qi took the throne, his title was lowered per precedent.

literal: Gang's younger brother Zhi; at the beginning of Zhuangdi's reign, Prince of Linyu, fief of one thousand households.
idiomatic: Gang's younger brother Zhi was Prince of Linyu at Zhuangdi's accession, with a thousand households.

literal: In the third year of Yong'an he died.
idiomatic: He died in Yong'an year 3.

literal: In the Deposed Emperor's time he was posthumously given General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Protocol of the Third Rank.
idiomatic: Under the Deposed Emperor he was posthumously general of chariots and cavalry, left grand master of splendid happiness, and protocol of the third rank.

literal: Shao's younger brother's son Zheng was handsome in appearance and by nature mild and broad.
idiomatic: Shao's nephew Zheng was handsome and mild by nature.

literal: At the beginning of Suzong's reign he was enfeoffed Duke of Bacheng, fief of one thousand households.
idiomatic: At Suzong's accession he was Duke of Bacheng with a thousand households.

literal: He served as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Vice Minister of Rites.
idiomatic: He served as scattered-cavalry attendant and vice minister of rites.

literal: When Zhuangdi took the throne he was made Minister over the Masses and enfeoffed Prince of Shiping.
idiomatic: At Zhuangdi's accession he was minister over the masses and Prince of Shiping.

literal: He and his elder brother Shao both met with disaster.
idiomatic: He and his elder brother Shao both met disaster.

literal: Posthumously given Acting Yellow Battle-Ax, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without, Grand General, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Xiang [5]—Prince as before; imperial carriage with nine tassels, yellow canopy with left streamer, front and rear feathered canopy and drum escort, a hundred tiger guards with swords of state; posthumous name: Upright.
idiomatic: Posthumously: acting yellow battle-ax, palace attendant, commander of all armies, grand general, recorder of the Masters of Writing, Xiang [5], prince as before; nine-tassel carriage, yellow canopy with left streamer, feathered escort, a hundred tiger guards; posthumous name Upright.

literal: Son Qin, styled Shidao, inherited.
idiomatic: Son Qin, styled Shidao, succeeded.

literal: In Wuding he was Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
idiomatic: In Wuding he was scattered-cavalry attendant.

literal: When Qi received the Mandate, his rank was reduced by precedent.
idiomatic: When Northern Qi took the throne, his title was lowered per precedent.

literal: The historian says: Prince Martial-Proclaimer took filial piety as his substance and planted conduct with loyalty; literary stratagem and martial strategy came from his own breast; in the Taihe era he was bound close—was it in vain!
idiomatic: The historian says: Prince Martial-Proclaimer made filial piety his substance and loyalty his conduct; literary and martial strategy came from his own breast; in the Taihe years he was bound close—not in vain.

literal: As for conduct in safety yet facing danger, integrity in sending off the past and dwelling in the present, the righteousness of the Duke of Zhou not being another, the loyalty of Huo Guang as a different surname—the affairs were combined in him.
idiomatic: Conduct safe in danger, integrity in sending off the past and dwelling in the present, Zhou's righteousness not being another's, Huo's loyalty though of different surname—all combined in him.

literal: Merit high enough to shake the ruler, virtue lofty enough to move custom—one slander entered, and in the end his will was not preserved.
idiomatic: Merit that shook the throne, virtue that moved custom—one whisper entered, and his will was not preserved.

literal: Alas!
idiomatic: Alas!
